Now the contract file for the new package. Writing the types myself so the engine and the `check` integration can be built against the same definitions.

Waiting on the plan reviewer. So far: branch `llm-review` created and `internal/review/types.go` written as the contract between the review engine and `slopcop check`. Implementation children start once the review comes back.

The review found real problems. My assessment:

- **#1/#2 (two separate captures, ignored policy files)**: valid, and it leads to a simpler design. Build one snapshot tree through the temporary index and derive both the service patch and the review diff from it. `WorkingTreePatch` keeps its signature, so its existing tests check that the patch is unchanged.
- **#3 (gate vs dirty-tree approval)**: valid. I'll approve the tree *without* force-added ignored policy files, because that is the tree a commit produces. The skill will explain that an approval covers this exact content.
- **#5 (top-level `status` misleads)**: valid. Top-level `status` will always match the exit code, plus a `staticStatus` field.
- **#6, #7, #10**: valid; adopted as suggested.
- **#4 (model matching)**: valid. The engine will mirror Mjolnir's option lookup. I will not authorize live adapter runs yet, because checkpoint's README notes that Codex adapter 2.5.0 can log out the shared login.
- **#9 (Windows)**: partly valid. Go can start `.cmd` files, but killing the whole process tree needs care. Using `taskkill /T /F` is simpler than attaching a job object.

Updating the plan with these changes.
Plan updated. Two additions to the contract before spawning: `Options` needs the mode (stored in `last.json`) and the slopcop version (part of the reuse key).

The report directories are ignored, so they will not enter checks. Waiting for the three children (snapshot, review engine, config). Next, once the config child releases `root.go`, I'll start the per-repository `init` + push gate slice.
